quest.title: The Continuation of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: You come to attend today's Sabzeruz Festival, but you are haunted by a lingering sense of déjà vu...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Primogem x30, Mora x25450, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You mean... The Akasha is causing our mental fatigue? Now that I think about it, my head's been feeling unusually heavy.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: When the desert-dwellers set off on their quest for knowledge, a sage once said, "Knowledge always comes at a price."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Compiling the entire country's knowledge...You think the Akasha pulled a 180 and is extracting information from us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But how would it do that...?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Who knows? The Akasha can put knowledge into our heads, so who's to say that it can't also poke around in there? We don't know any specifics.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the point of doing something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just think about it... If you could combine the knowledge of every single person in Sumeru, then you can basically turn Sumeru City into a single, massive brain...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...This hivemind could make breakthroughs in problems that even the smartest geniuses can't crack.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: An excellent deduction. And the analogy comparing Sumeru City to a massive brain? Ahh, I love it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, we should take off our Akasha Terminals right away! Maybe that'll solve this problem?

choices.text: It's worth a shot.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah. I was only wearing this for show in the first place. Didn't expect the Sages to cook up such a conspiracy... Mark my words, when this is over, I'm getting evidence and exposing this whole thing to the public!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone removes their Akasha Terminals...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How does everyone feel?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Actually, I also noticed something else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What is it?

choices.text: I feel like at the end of every day...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that! Paimon knows what you're talking about! It's a single, soft beep that sounds like it's coming from the Akasha Terminal.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: The sound of a beep... Could it be a prompt tone for when the Akasha is operating?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I heard the same sound in Port Ormos.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's probably an important clue. We weren't using our terminals, but we heard a beep anyway...
*beep*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Traveler, did you hear that!?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I heard it, too! Our ears aren't messing with us. There was definitely a beep, but it sounded like it was coming from inside my head!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: We took off our Akasha Terminals... How...?
Phase runtime has exceeded its expected length. At this rate, there may be casualties...
But... we cannot lose all of our progress.

choices.text: There is always the sound of a beep.
Somehow, I don't think it'll be that simple.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Why does Paimon feel so tired after so much sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, we should go meet Dunyarzad right away.

talks.objective: Go to the appointed place and talk to Dunyarzad

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good morning, Dunyarzad! Sorry to keep you waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Not at all. I arrived early.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon thinks you sound kinda tired... Did you not get enough sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm doing well. There's no need to worry. Shall we go? Let's start with the stalls over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great idea! Let's get going. Traveler... Uh, hey, Traveler?

choices.text: This feels... all too familiar.
What a strong sense of déjà vu...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Haha, it's all thanks to Miss Dunyarzad's sponsorship that the children can enjoy the Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Oh, are you interested in Yalda Candies? I have some boxes of candy here. Pick whichever one you want.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, not much of a choice... All these boxes look the same.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Haha, it's not that simple. Each box contains a random flavor — it's up to the luck of the draw. Flavors include Lavender Melon, Harra Fruit, Sunsettia...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm-hmm~ They all sound pretty tasty.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: ...And there's also Lizard Tail and Onikabuto.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? What were those last two!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... {F#She'll}{M#He'll} help me choose. Paimon wants the Sunsettia flavor!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: No problem. These boxes of candy are numbered one to five from left to right. Which one do you want?

choices.text: Number four.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Oho? I like your confidence — no hesitation at all. Ah, congratulations! Number four is indeed Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Haha, Paimon knew {F#she}{M#he} always had incredible luck!

choices.text: Number one is Lizard Tail.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm, Paimon's not really interested in the other flavors.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Ah... W—Wait, how did you know? Don't tell me that you already knew which flavor was in each box?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What? {F#She}{M#He} was right about all of them?

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: That couldn't have been luck. H—How is this possible? I packed all those boxes this morning, and they've been sealed ever since. You couldn't have known beforehand.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: ...Mind reading? X-ray vision? Or some kind of magic trick? This is way too freaky...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tell us what's going on! Since when did you get superpowers... Traveler?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just now, that was...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Where are you going?

choices.text: Number two is Harra Fruit.
Number three is Lavender Melon.
Number five is Onikabuto.
Number four.
Number four.
Number four.
Number four.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you looking for? Why did we come here?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A familiar figure... An overwhelming sense of déjà vu...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: A time loop... *sigh* You've given similarly wrong answers in the past. A pity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still the wrong answer... Paimon thought that made a lot of sense! It feels like time's just repeating itself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: A simple time loop can't explain some of the phenomena. You two are still missing a lot of information. Unfortunately, I can't give you any more hints...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Sabzeruz Festival is happening every day, but that doesn't mean we can waste an infinite amount of them. Hurry and find the truth before today's festival ends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's think about our current situation... To save Dunyarzad, we have to escape the samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And to do that, we need to figure out what's happening — the "truth"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida rejected the idea of a time loop, so we must have missed something, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's memories say that we've already done this many times, but... let's go talk to people again. It's more productive than sitting here and scratching our heads... Why don't we start with... those stall owners?

talks.objective: Ask around for clues about the current situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there!

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: Hey, it's you guys again. Where's your cultured friend?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She... She's feeling a little unwell.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I see. Did you come back to buy something? I guarantee the freshness of my products. I harvested them from the forest just yesterday.

choices.text: Have you felt anything strange lately?

response.speaker: Amal
response.text: Huh? What brought this about? I hurried back from the forest yesterday, and I'm selling produce here today. I haven't felt anything strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... To put it another way, if you really, really think about it, was "yesterday" truly "yesterday"? Did you actually come back from the forest yesterday?

response.speaker: Amal
response.text: What kind of philosophical nonsense is this? Are you two daydreaming?

response.speaker: Amal
response.text: Didn't you know that no one dreams in Sumeru? Go somewhere else if you want to find someone to daydream with, hahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... He actually has a point. Is this a dream? Is everyone dreaming?

choices.text: Remember what he said just now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm, true. It's so weird that people here don't dream! Why is that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, if this all really were just a dream, we would've woken up a long time ago. Let's keep asking around.

choices.text: No one dreams in Sumeru.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the same day?

talks.objective: Ask around for clues about the current situation

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two! Was my divination so accurate that you felt compelled to compliment me in person?

choices.text: We actually did run into a situation.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Oooh, I knew it! I told you, the gods' divination is highly accurate. You just hadn't fully understood its significance yet. Hahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're really excited about this, huh... That's exactly why we came back. Help us better understand it!

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Er... Help you better understand it...? W—Well, that isn't exactly what I excel at...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're admitting that you don't have a clue?

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Anyway, what kind of situation did you get into?

choices.text: We're all trapped in the day of the Sabzeruz Festival.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Huh? Hold on a second... I thought you guys just lost your wallet or fell for a scam...

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: What you just said... Are you serious? Does that kind of thing actually happen in real life?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knew you weren't going to believe it!

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: Marvelous, truly marvelous... I believe you. Recall the interpretation of your divination... The Moon, illusions, and lies... It really felt like an omen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you say it like that, the divination does sound like it's related to what's going on. Can you read any more into it?

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: I believe that the Archon's revelations are never more than vague hints. Anything more specific is beyond the reach of mere mortals.

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: The book only says, "If you trust your instincts and overcome your fears, the sun will surely rise."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is... Looks like fortune-telling is just fortune-telling — it's no good for practical problems.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We haven't made any progress. Who else can we talk to?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's try talking to Dehya again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm, Paimon remembers that we've tried talking to her a couple of times, but she always thinks that we're playing pranks on her. You think she'll brush us off again?

choices.text: She cares a lot about Dunyarzad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... If we tap into Dehya's strong sense of responsibility as a mercenary, then she'll definitely take us seriously.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At this time of day, Dehya's probably just finished beating up those kidnappers. Let's go find her!

choices.text: Let's try taking her to see the real Dunyarzad.
You've actually divined our fortune many, many times.
But I'm not sure if it's related to your divination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tell her, Traveler!

choices.text: You got injured because you aren't used to your current greatsword.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I didn't tell anyone about that, including Miss Dunyarzad. You couldn't have known... And just now, you literally took the words right out of my mouth. What's going on?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, so this is the situation...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain everything to Dehya...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's kinda hard to believe what you just told me... First, let me make something clear: Most of us desert-dwellers might not be the scholarly type, but we do have basic common sense...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Haven't you noticed something off about Dunyarzad?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's quieter than usual, uninterested in anything, and really gloomy...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, she isn't the same as before, but...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Her parents said that this is how she was like at first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? At first?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I don't quite understand what you are all talking about. I'll go rest on the bench over there.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My lady... Are you angry...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Come with me. I'll show you some evidence.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Alright. I'll give you the benefit of the doubt since you knew about my greatsword. Let's make this a quick trip — Miss Dunyarzad isn't completely safe here.

choices.text: You sold your greatsword to support the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...I'm fine, my lady. It's just a scratch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Perfect timing! Both of you are here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Paimon, Traveler, you came at just the right time! Listen, there was a dangerous—

choices.text: A gang of kidnappers had just ambushed you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Huh, you saw? Then why didn't you jump in earlier? If someone was protecting Miss Dunyarzad, I could've went all-out. Anyway, can you do something for me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You want the Traveler to take Dunyarzad somewhere to rest up while you check to see if there are still any kidnappers around. Did Paimon get that right?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...How did you know what I was going to say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need to say something convincing...

choices.text: You just defeated a gang of kidnappers.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: This is divine wisdom...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Any more requests, young soldiers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! That's... Isn't that Dunyarzad!?

choices.text: What!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's happening here? Why are there two Dunyarzads?
You already know that this isn't your first Sabzeruz Festival, don't you?
I'm sure you already know how to use this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Knowledge Capsule? Where did you get it...? What's inside?
You should use it too, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Y—You know Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, this seems kinda sketchy, but... Paimon feels like this is what we should do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What the!?

choices.text: Memories!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is our twentieth time at the Sabzeruz Festival? Hmm, no... The thirtieth? Fortieth? Just how many times have we been to the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have we been trapped in a single day? If it weren't for you, we wouldn't have even realized...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the heck was inside that Knowledge Capsule?
Your memories are still scrambled? Try your best to remember. This isn't the first time we've met, and I answered that question a long time ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Let Paimon think... Ohh, it's coming back... Meeting you was the real catalyst for restoring our memories, and... the Knowledge Capsule was just your means of showing our minds the way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about everyone else? Why are you only helping the two of us?
Your sense of déjà vu is stronger than everyone else's, yes? As for an explanation... You two received the blessing of Dendro, and you also have special, sensitive constitutions.
It was as if a single sheet of paper was separating those memories from your consciousness.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's wrong with the Dunyarzad over there...?
A familiar question. I think this is the seventh time you asked that.
As you can see, she isn't doing well. You probably sensed it, too — the Dunyarzad you were just with is different from the first Dunyarzad you met.
That "first" Dunyarzad is in front of you right now, and... she doesn't have a lot of time left.

choices.text: What I need to do right now is...

response.text: Hehe, looks like you're almost done sorting out your brain.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh yeah, I'm Nahida.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know; you introduced yourself before.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Good, you passed the test.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's happening...? You can awaken our memories, and you seem like you know what's going on... Wait, please don't tell Paimon even you don't know!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Everything in this world runs in a loop... This cycle is called a "samsara." You, me, and everyone else are all stuck inside a one-day samsara...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As for the truth... That's on you to find out. If you were told the truth instead of discovering it yourselves... It would literally blow your minds. I don't know how you'd be after that.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I can only give you surface-level help, like bits of information and subtle hints. For the rest of the time, I'll be doing all I can to slow down Dunyarzad's illness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She looks like she isn't doing well at all... Her illness gets worse after each Sabzeruz Festival...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If we can break out of this samsara, I might be able to save her.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...But as things are right now, she's just a small bird in the sky that's about to lose its last feathers. All I can do is raise a gale to delay her fall.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure love to use weird analogies.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Analogies are wonderful tools. They let you use existing knowledge to understand unfamiliar things.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay, so... With what you know so far, what do you think the truth is?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm... Let me collect my thoughts...

choices.text: Break out of this cycle...?
So many days' worth of memories...
Let's use it together, Paimon.
(Alert)
She was still with us just a moment ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, we brought a friend. Are you busy?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...I thought I told you that it won't help to bring anyone here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just wanted her to see the real Dunyarzad's condition...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The real Dunyarzad? ...Where? And who are you talking to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: *sigh* I told you that you two are special. Other people can't see me or Miss Dunyarzad here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hold on... Over there, is that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Y—You can see her?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wow, how perceptive... Does she have invisible antennae?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Miss Dunyarzad... she's lying down here, isn't she? How's she doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Her condition's really bad, and she's basically in a coma. How did you know she was here?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I can sense her aura... There are also lingering feelings of something like regret or disappointment. What happened...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you believe us now? The Sabzeruz Festival has been repeating itself...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You begin discussing the issue with Dehya, who finally understands the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So you think the sages are behind this?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah. They've always been against us. It wouldn't surprise me if they're using the Akasha to intentionally repeat the Sabzeruz Festival as a sick joke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, you have a point... Aside from the Dendro Archon, the Akademiya's sages are the only ones in Sumeru who could pull off something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe there's more to the Akasha than we know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nahida, can you tell us anything about the Akasha?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Didn't you awaken our memories using something that looked like a Knowledge Capsule? That means you must know something about the Akasha!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Gnosis can do that!? No wonder the Akasha is so magical — it's being powered by the Gnosis of Sumeru's Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So, this Nahida you mentioned... What did she say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said, and Paimon quotes: "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and grants knowledge to the people... Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I get the "grants knowledge" part — that's what people have always used the Akasha for. But compiling the entire populace's wisdom? How does that work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did she mean that the sages enter new knowledge into the Akasha?

choices.text: Doubt it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, that sounds about right. What do you think?

choices.text: Most information in the Akasha comes from Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You all seem to have a matter to attend to. Don't worry about me. I'll be sitting here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on? Did you see something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Us leaving Dunyarzad without letting her know is kinda rude, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Moon, illusions, and lies... What do they all mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's happening right now seems to have happened before. This feeling has been getting stronger and stronger...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage said, "Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content." Did he mean something more?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dehya sold her greatsword to raise additional funds, and then she was injured because she wasn't used to her new weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My mind feels exhausted, even though I haven't done too much thinking. What is going on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've already experienced the Sabzeruz Festival many times. And... the day of the festival seems to be in a perpetual samsara.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: People in Sumeru don't dream. What a strange phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, Nahida said, "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mercenaries rely heavily on muscle memory. And Dehya was able to use her experiences to avoid injury in later samsara cycles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations. We still hear it every night, even though we removed our Akasha Terminals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the bizarre spaces I saw outside the city had one thing in common: a lack of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces remind me of... dreams. Like the one I had in the Avidya Forest, except these have no sign of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces kept disappearing before my eyes, but as soon as that beep sounded, many more spaces materialized.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those dreamscapes kept vanishing, but as soon as that beep sounded, more new spaces appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ..Was that space actually the real world? But wouldn't a real space just randomly disappearing like that be catastrophic?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My impression is that each day in this samsara only ends at the sound of that beep from the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That should be it... The flow of time is endlessly cycling within one single day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If all our memories of a day are erased at the end of that day, then we would unwittingly relive the same day again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We are all in a dream. It isn't that the people of Sumeru don't dream. Rather, the Akasha is taking their dreams from them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It is a manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And it grants knowledge to the people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They say that alchemical divination is the Dendro Archon's divine revelation. So then, if Nahida has referred to herself as the Moon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" a hint that we're all dreaming?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" hinting at the Sages' deception of Sumeru's people?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to carefully think things through...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... I can't seem to cohesively piece everything together.
